transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (SE), Diego Alvarez (CSM); Evelyn Park (Head of Platform), Samir Patel (CTO), Jules Moreno (Infra), Anya Li (Security)

Summary (auto): align scope for pilot and staging; collect network/KMS details; send security pack and runbook; schedule pilot kickoff.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood inference, i'll run the agenda quick — intro, success criteria, staging plan, security sync, and next steps. priya and diego are with me.
[00:18] Evelyn: hi all, thanks — i'll jump in for Ridgewave; Samir and Jules and Anya are here, we're trying to validate inference latency across our checkout flows and want to avoid ballooning cost.
[00:30] Priya: great, quick note — our typical onboarding split is 1) confirm success metrics 2) staging access and perf benchmarks 3) pilot with small production traffic and rollout. is that close to what you had in mind?
[00:45] Samir: yeah that's fine. our main constraints: must sit inside our VPC, we have strict KMS controls for PII, and the finance team will want predictable pricing.
[01:05] Diego: noted — we usually recommend a short pilot on Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private depending on VPC/keys. we'll map options after the staging results.
[01:22] Jules: quick question — when you say 'private' do you mean full on-prem or VPC peering? we prefer peering, we can't ship on-prem boxes right now.
[01:35] Priya: good call — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed network paths; on-prem is optional but typically more for air-gapped and regulated. for your use-case VPC peering + BYOK KMS should be workable.
[01:52] Anya: when you say BYOK, do you integrate with AWS KMS imported keys or do we need HSM? we have an HSM-backed KMS in account.
[02:05] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS and can work with external HSM providers; in some setups we ask for a key policy that allows Redwood's runtime role to encrypt/decrypt ephemeral model cache items — we can send a sample policy.
[02:24] Samir: ok sample policy would help. also we care about cold-start latencies on our shortest path — sub 150ms token times ideally — is that realistic?
[02:40] Priya: depends on model size and sequence lengths. for smaller LLMs on recent GPUs Redwood often hits tail latencies under 80ms per token for single-turn short sequences; larger models or long conversations push that up. we will include latency profiles in the runbook.
[02:58] Maya: can we align on what success looks like? metrics, SLAs, and timeline — Samir?
[03:10] Samir: success = 95th percentile latency <200ms on our common prompt set + cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll share a target) and SOC2 compliance evidence. timeline: pilot within 2 weeks if staging access is straightforward.
[03:30] Diego: great — we'll aim for pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-25. priya will provide the benchmark scripts and acceptance tests so you can run them in staging.
[03:45] Jules: about staging, what network egress is needed? we have strict egress nat rules.
[03:53] Priya: for VPC peering we only need port 443 outbound-ish for control-plane? (some customers put restrictions). we also provide an option for private endpoints if you want to avoid public egress. i'll detail both.
[04:10] Anya: audit logs — what level of logs do you provide? we need request-level tracing to satisfy our audit team.
[04:20] Diego: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, trace ids, and per-route latency. for Private we can enable longer retention and push logs to your S3 or SIEM via secure delivery.
[04:36] Evelyn: will logs contain PII? we plan to strip PII before sending but we want to be sure logs don't accidentally persist full user inputs.
[04:48] Priya: by default we redact prompts in hosted flows, but in Private mode we can follow your retention policy. we'll share the redaction and retention docs.
[05:00] [ambient noise, brief pause]
[05:10] Samir: another question - model pinning & rollbacks. we need a way to pin a model version and have automatic fallback in case of regression.
[05:20] Priya: yep, Redwood supports model pinning per route and automatic fallback policies to compatible variants. rollouts can be canary/A-B. we'll show this in the demo.
[05:35] Jules: on quantization — are you recommending 4-bit for us? we aim to cut cost but maintain quality.
[05:42] Priya: often 4-bit works well for embeddings and some generation models, but you'll want A/B tests. Priya: (laughter) we'll include quantization profiles and observed quality regressions in the runbook.
[05:58] Maya: let's switch to staging logistics — what accounts and network info do you need from Ridgewave?
[06:06] Jules: we'll provide AWS account IDs and an IAM contact, plus CIDR ranges. we might need an allowlist for a small set of Redwood IPs.
[06:16] Priya: perfect — we'll provide an allowlist template and peering docs. also we'll need a short list of prompts for your acceptance test and a sample traffic profile for the pilot.
[06:31] Anya: about encryption at rest — if we use customer-managed KMS, does Redwood still cache KV data on GPUs? how's that encrypted?
[06:43] Priya: Good call — KV caches on runtime are ephemeral; at rest we encrypt model artifacts and persistent caches with your KMS keys when in Private mode. for Dedicated we can offer encrypted volumes and controlled access. i'll add a short section on runtime encryption to the security pack.
[06:59] [09:00] Maya: (to Diego) maybe we should propose a small 2-week pilot: week 1 staging + benchmarks, week 2 low-traffic ramp. Thoughts?
[09:12] Diego: yep that's exactly our usual plan. we'll make the pilot scoped: up to X tokens/day to validate latency/cost.
[09:23] Samir: fine, as long as we can stop or pause if costs spike. who owns throttling?
[09:28] Priya: Redwood provides rate limits and per-route quotas; you can set application-level throttles. we'll also recommend autoscaling policies for Dedicated that cap burst spend.
[09:40] Evelyn: do you have any customers in retail with similar traffic patterns we can reference?
[09:47] Maya: yes, we have a retail customer reference (internal note - we'll anonymize) and a benchmark doc; i'll include one pager.
[09:58] Jules: about observability — can we stream traces to our datadog?
[10:03] Priya: we support exporting traces via OTLP to Datadog or your APM; we'll include config snippets.
[10:12] Anya: SSO and RBAC — we run SAML SSO and need role based controls for dev/test/prod teams.
[10:20] Diego: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and RBAC with fine-grained roles; in Private mode we can sync groups from your IdP.
[10:31] [10:40] Samir: pricing — can we get an estimate for a Dedicated reserved pool vs hosted per-token costs?
[10:47] Maya: yes i'll send a comparison table after this call with commit tiers and burst options. for pilot we'll propose a short reserved window or hosted to reduce time to test.
[10:58] Jules: one last infra question — do you need us to install anything in our VPC?
[11:04] Priya: typically no agent required; we rely on VPC peering and private endpoints. for very strict envs some customers run a lightweight sidecar to handle egress policies, but that's optional.
[11:18] [12:00] Maya: ok quick recap of agreed items — we need: Ridgewave to share account IDs, CIDRs, KMS contact; Anya to share compliance doc checklist; Priya to share runbook and benchmark scripts; Maya to send security pack and pricing. everyone ok?
[12:35] Evelyn: yes that works.
[12:40] Samir: ok.
[12:45] Anya: will you also share the sample key policy for AWS KMS?
[12:50] Priya: yes, sample key policy + minimum permissions, we'll attach that to the security pack.
[13:02] [13:30] Jules: small comment about fallback: we need a plan if a model update causes hallucination spikes — do you support automated rollback based on quality alerts?
[13:43] Priya: yes — Redwood Optimize can trigger regressions based on eval sets and roll back or fallback to a previous variant; we'll configure alerts tied to your prompt set.
[13:58] Samir: perfect. cost control again — can you throttle at token-level?
[14:06] Diego: yes per-key quotas and rate limits exist and we can create budget alerts.
[14:15] [15:00] Maya: moving on — timeline and next calendar items: we'll aim to have the security pack and runbook in 3 business days, pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-25. i'll create the calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[15:25] Evelyn: thanks. one operational ask — can we have a 1-hour deep-dive SE session once staging is up? Jules and Anya will join.
[15:34] Priya: absolutely, happy to run a focused deep dive.
[15:40] Maya: action items recap — i'll send notes, Diego will schedule kickoff, priya will share docs. any blockers?
[15:48] Anya: none from security besides confirming the docs.
[15:52] Samir: none.
[16:00] [ambient keyboard clicking and small cross-talk]
[16:20] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments.
[16:27] Evelyn: thanks all. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and auto-caption errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache) remain; speaker attribution may be approximate for 1-2 lines.

Attachments referenced: security-pack-link (will be sent post-call), staging-runbook-draft (to be provided by Priya), pilot-benchmark-sheet (to be provided).
